title: Learn the Shim Sham - for Lindy Hop and Swing Dance

extraction.teacher_style: Laura Glaess breaks down the Shim Sham step-by-step with clear verbal guidance and visual demonstrations. She emphasizes rhythm, body mechanics, and musicality while encouraging personal expression.

lesson_structure.note: Laura introduces herself and the dance.
Shows footage of people dancing the Shim Sham in various settings.
Explains the timing and counts of the main body of the Shim Sham.
Demonstrates move number one: Shim Sham.
Demonstrates building move number two: Cross Over and Pushes.
Demonstrates building move number three: Tack Annie.
Demonstrates building move number four: Half Break.
Gives pointers on footwork and technique for the Shim Sham and Tack Annie.
Dances through the entire routine with music and voiceover cues.

common_mistakes: making steps too big instead of using rhythm
being too upright during stomp-off instead of using body movement
making the kick too big instead of letting the movement do the work

steps_taught.name: Shim Sham
steps_taught.description: The foundational step of the routine starting on eight.

steps_taught.name: Cross Over
steps_taught.description: Crossing feet over during the movement.

steps_taught.name: Pushes
steps_taught.description: Pushing movement incorporated into the choreography.

steps_taught.name: Tack Annie
steps_taught.description: A rhythmic footwork movement featuring a stomp off.

steps_taught.name: Half Break
steps_taught.description: A transitional break step in the dance.

what_works: dancing along with verbal reminders during music practice
what_hinders: lack of back or side angle demonstrations during the footwork breakdown

quotes.text: You are a dancer before you are a partner dancer.
The main body of the Shim Sham consists of only four moves.
Keep in mind this comes from tap.
